name: Kalsubai Peak
description: Maharashtra's highest peak at 1,646m, near Bhandardara. A steady climb through five iron ladders with sweeping Sahyadri views from the summit temple.
highlights: Five iron-ladder sections leading up to the summit
360° Sahyadri views from Maharashtra's highest point
Sunrise treks are popular — starts pre-dawn from Bari
how_to_reach: Drive to Bari village via Igatpuri or Bhandardara road; trailhead starts from Bari.
nearest_station: Kasara Railway Station — 40 km; taxis run on to Bari village.
safety_note: The iron ladders near the top get crowded and slippery in monsoon — climb one at a time and hold the rails.

faqs.question: Is Kalsubai suitable for beginners?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a fitness base — it's rated moderate and the ladders are the only technical part.

faqs.question: How long does the climb take?
faqs.answer: 4-5 hours up from Bari village, and roughly the same coming down.

faqs.question: Is it crowded?
faqs.answer: Very, especially on weekends and around sunrise — it's Maharashtra's most-climbed peak.

faqs.question: Best time to go?
faqs.answer: October to February for clear skies; monsoon adds risk on the ladder sections.

name: Rajmachi Trek
description: Twin forts (Shrivardhan and Manaranjan) reached via a forested trail from Lonavala, popular for monsoon greenery and a night trek option.
how_to_reach: From Lonavala, drive/hike to Udhewadi base village via Tungarli or Kondhane route.

name: Harishchandragad
description: A demanding climb to an ancient hill fort, famous for the Konkan Kada cliff and the Kedareshwar cave temple.
highlights: Konkan Kada — a massive concave cliff, rare "sun's halo" cloud effect at sunrise
Kedareshwar cave — giant Shivling ringed by knee-deep water
Popular overnight-camping summit under a wide-open night sky
how_to_reach: Base villages Khireshwar or Pachnai, reached via Kalyan-Ahmednagar road.
nearest_station: Igatpuri Railway Station — 38 km; taxis run on to Khireshwar base village.
safety_note: Konkan Kada's edge has no railing and gets foggy — stay well back, especially at dawn. The Pachnai route has a risky rock-patch in the rains.

faqs.question: Is Harishchandragad safe for beginners?
faqs.answer: No — it's rated hard. The Konkan Kada cliff and the long approach make it unsuitable for first-time trekkers.

faqs.question: How long does the trek take?
faqs.answer: 7-8 hours one way from Khireshwar or Pachnai; most groups make it an overnight trek.

faqs.question: Is water available on the trail?
faqs.answer: Yes, near Kedareshwar cave and at the top — but carry your own for the climb up.

faqs.question: Can I drive close to the base?
faqs.answer: Yes — both Khireshwar and Pachnai villages are motorable; the trek starts from there.

faqs.question: Best time to visit?
faqs.answer: October to February for clear views. Avoid monsoon — the rock sections get slippery.

name: Sinhagad Fort
description: An easy, popular trek right outside Pune with a motorable road option too, known for kanda bhaji and hilltop views.
how_to_reach: Drive from Pune via Khadakwasla to the base, then a short climb or road to the top.

name: Lohagad Fort
description: A beginner-friendly fort trek near Lonavala with a stepped path, monsoon waterfalls en route, and the famous Vinchu Kata spur.
how_to_reach: From Malavli station or Lonavala, drive to Lohagadwadi base village.

name: Kondhari Waterfall
description: A tucked-away waterfall near Bhor, gushing hard through the monsoon with a short walk from the nearest road.
how_to_reach: Drive to Bhor via NH4, then follow local roads toward the falls.

name: Tamhini Waterfall
description: Roadside and trail waterfalls through the Tamhini Ghat, one of the greenest monsoon drives near Pune.
how_to_reach: Drive from Pune via Mulshi towards Tamhini Ghat road.

name: Devkund Waterfall
description: A two-tiered waterfall near Bhira reached by a river-crossing trail through the forest, one of the tallest in the region.
how_to_reach: Drive to Bhira village, then trek roughly 5km along the stream to the falls.

name: Randha Falls
description: A dramatic horseshoe-shaped waterfall near Bhandardara, easily viewable from a roadside deck.
how_to_reach: On the main Bhandardara road, a short walk from the parking area.

name: Pawna Lake Camping
description: The classic Mumbai-Pune weekend campsite: lakeside tents facing Tikona and Lohagad forts, with bonfires and DJ nights on weekends.
how_to_reach: Drive via Lonavala or Kamshet to the Pawna Dam backwater campsites.

name: Bhandardara Camping
description: Quiet lakeside camping by Arthur Lake at the base of Kalsubai, with pine groves and cleaner night skies than most weekend spots.
how_to_reach: Drive via Igatpuri or Sangamner to Bhandardara village and the lakeside camps.

name: Kamshet Camping
description: Hillside campsites known for sunrise paragliding, overlooking the Indrayani valley near Lonavala.
how_to_reach: Drive to Kamshet on the old Mumbai-Pune highway, campsites are a short climb off the road.

name: Rajmachi Camping
description: Tent stays at Udhewadi village beneath Rajmachi fort, popular for a combined monsoon trek-and-camp weekend.
how_to_reach: Drive/hike from Lonavala to Udhewadi village, campsites are run by local homestays.

name: Kalavantin Durg
description: A dramatic rock pinnacle beside Prabalgad fort, reached via ancient rock-cut steps carved into a near-vertical cliff face — one of the most photographed and most dangerous treks in the Sahyadris.
highlights: The final rock-cut staircase — steep, narrow steps carved into the cliff with no railing
360° views over Prabalgad, Matheran and the Konkan plains from the pinnacle top
One of the most photographed treks near Mumbai, especially at sunrise
how_to_reach: Drive or train to Panvel, then bus or taxi to Thakurwadi village (~15 km); the climb to Prabalgad and Kalavantin starts from there.
nearest_station: Panvel Railway Station — 15 km; buses run to Thakurwadi village.
safety_note: The final rock-cut staircase is narrow, steep and unprotected on one side — fatal falls have been reported here. Avoid in monsoon or wet conditions, and don't attempt it if you're uncomfortable with exposure.

faqs.question: Is Kalavantin Durg dangerous?
faqs.answer: Yes — the final rock-cut staircase has caused fatal falls in the past. It's unprotected, steep, and not suitable for beginners or anyone uncomfortable with heights.

faqs.question: How long does the trek take?
faqs.answer: About 3-4 hours one way from Thakurwadi village, including the steep final climb.

faqs.question: Best time to visit?
faqs.answer: October to February for dry, stable rock. Avoid monsoon — the steps get slippery and windy.

faqs.question: Can beginners attempt this trek?
faqs.answer: Not recommended. The approach to Prabalgad is moderate, but the Kalavantin pinnacle climb itself is technical and risky for inexperienced trekkers.

name: Karnala Bird Sanctuary
description: A bird sanctuary on the old Mumbai-Goa highway with an easy fort-top trek inside it — a good beginner trek and a well-known birdwatching spot in one visit.
highlights: Karnala Fort's pinnacle, a short easy climb inside the sanctuary
Over 150 resident and migratory bird species, best seen Nov-Feb
A good half-day trek for beginners and families
how_to_reach: On the old Mumbai-Goa highway (NH66) near Panvel; buses run from the Panvel ST depot every 30 minutes.
nearest_station: Panvel Railway Station — 12 km; buses run every 30 min to Karnala.

faqs.question: Is this trek suitable for beginners?
faqs.answer: Yes — it's rated easy and a common choice for first-time trekkers and families.

faqs.question: What's the entry fee?
faqs.answer: ₹30 per adult at the sanctuary entrance.

faqs.question: What are the visiting hours?
faqs.answer: The entry checkpoint is open 7am-1pm; visitors should be back down by 4pm.

faqs.question: Is it good for birdwatching?
faqs.answer: Yes, though sightings vary by season — November to February is best for migratory birds.

name: Adai Waterfall
description: A two-stage seasonal waterfall a short walk from Adai village, with a natural plunge pool at the base — a monsoon-only spot popular for a quick swim.
highlights: A two-stage fall with a natural pool at the base, good for a monsoon dip
Only a 15-minute walk from Adai village — one of the easiest waterfalls near Panvel
Lush green forest walk in monsoon
how_to_reach: From Panvel, drive via the Kalamboli circle and the Adai road flyover to Adai village, or take an autorickshaw from Panvel or Khandeshwar station.
nearest_station: Khandeshwar Railway Station — 5 km; Panvel Railway Station — 4 km.
safety_note: This is a monsoon-only waterfall with a natural pool — rocks get slippery and flow can be strong after heavy rain, so check conditions before swimming.

faqs.question: When is the best time to visit?
faqs.answer: June to September, during monsoon — it's a seasonal waterfall and mostly dry the rest of the year.

faqs.question: Is there an entry fee?
faqs.answer: No, it's free to visit.

faqs.question: How far is the walk to the falls?
faqs.answer: About 15 minutes from Adai village.

faqs.question: Can I swim there?
faqs.answer: There's a natural plunge pool, but check the water flow first — it gets strong after heavy rain.

name: Kharghar Hills
description: A popular short hike right inside Navi Mumbai, with a summit that looks over the Kharghar valley, golf course and — on a clear evening — sunset over the Arabian Sea.
duration_label: 1.5-2 hr one way to the top
highlights: Sunrise to the east and sunset over the Arabian Sea from the same summit
One of the most accessible hill treks in Navi Mumbai — no long drive needed
Views of Kharghar dam, the golf course and the city skyline
how_to_reach: Take the harbour line to Kharghar or CBD Belapur station, then an auto to Sector 35 or the Owe Dam entry point at the base of the hill.
nearest_station: Kharghar Railway Station — 3 km; auto to Sector 35 or the Owe Dam entry point.
safety_note: Local authorities advise trekking only between 7 AM and 3 PM — avoid being on the hill after dark.

faqs.question: How do I get to the trailhead?
faqs.answer: Take a train to Kharghar or CBD Belapur station, then an auto to Sector 35 or the Owe Dam entry point.

faqs.question: Is there an entry fee?
faqs.answer: No, it's free and open 24x7, though trekking after dark isn't advised.

faqs.question: How long is the trek?
faqs.answer: About 1.5-2 hours one way to the summit.

faqs.question: Is it good for sunset?
faqs.answer: Yes — the summit faces west toward the Arabian Sea, one of the better sunset spots in Navi Mumbai.
